skins.name: Bootstrap 5 (Dracula look)
skins.description: The migration skin: a Bootstrap 5 + Dracula foundation (dracula.css + its reference component set), translated onto the t-* vocabulary. Bootstrap 5.3 metrics (control padding, 6px radius, 1.5 line-height, system font stack) in pure CSS; nothing vendored.
skins.notes: Pure CSS translation of dracula.css + reference/*.css: every --drac-* became its --t-* token, every rgba() tint a color-mix() of the tone. Bootstrap itself is not vendored: that foundation already overrode nearly every Bootstrap default, Bootstrap's class selectors cannot be aliased onto tailor attributes without re-declaring anyway, and its JS is unusable under the no-JS rule. Icons: projects using tailor typically use Bootstrap Icons in .t-icon slots; the skin does not depend on them. Light mode checked with Dracula/Alucard; dark with Dracula and Gruvbox.

skins.name: daisyUI 5
skins.description: daisyUI 5.7.50's look (pill buttons with a press-down translate, soft rounded-box cards and modals, chunky squircle-thumb toggles, tabs-box segmented controls, soft-tint badges and alerts, the SVG-mask loading ring) translated onto the t-* vocabulary, every colour read from --t-* tokens.
skins.notes: Not vendored: daisyUI 5 is a Tailwind 4 CSS plugin whose component classes (btn, badge, modal-box…) cannot be demanded from read-only tailor markup (contract rule 5), and its colours are OKLCH --color-* theme tokens. The relevant declarations from its built CSS were re-expressed against t-* selectors; base-100→canvas, base-200→inset/selection, base-300→border, base-content→text, primary→accent, neutral→overlay-bg. Muted text uses daisy's trick of color-mix'ing base-content at 45–60 % instead of a second palette colour.

skins.name: GOV.UK Frontend (translated)
skins.description: GOV.UK Frontend's form language on the t-* vocabulary: 2px square borders, no radius, the fat 3px focus block in a warning-derived accent, bold labels above fields, 5px error bar on invalid fields, big solid buttons with the bottom shadow line, inset-text alerts, uppercase tinted tags, summary-list settings rows and GOV.UK tables. Light-first by birth, token-driven so dark palettes read.
skins.notes: Translated, not vendored: GOV.UK Frontend styles per-class (govuk-*) with hard-coded hex for buttons, tags, inputs and the header, and sets no body font; aliasing it onto tailor markup would need the markup to change (SKIN-CONTRACT rule 5). Declarations are re-expressed on t-* selectors. Licence: GDS Transport font and the crown/GOV.UK wordmark are gov.uk-only, so the skin uses the system sans stack and draws no crown or logo anywhere. Focus: GOV.UK's #ffdd00 is a colour literal and therefore banned; the focus block is color-mix(--t-warning 70%, --t-hue-yellow) with --t-overlay-bg/--t-canvas-derived text, visible on both modes. GOV.UK has no dark mode, no toasts, menus, tooltips, cards, switches or sidebar; those are composed in its idiom (notification-banner toasts, bordered summary cards, square checkbox-style switch, 5px-bordered dialog like the timeout pattern).

skins.name: luz (d00m-gui)
skins.description: @d00m-gui/luz 0.5.0 translated onto the t-* vocabulary: scheme-tinted soft fills over outlines, depth-shifted nested surfaces, pill badges, boxed field groups, segmented tabs, notice-style toasts — troopy's feel. luz's OKLCH ramp maths cannot run per-palette, so depth is approximated with decaying color-mix() steps of --t-text into --t-canvas, enumerated over three nesting levels like luz's own _depth.css.
skins.notes: Translation, not a vendoring (luz is distributed as a release tarball, not on npm; its component CSS depends on generated OKLCH ramp tokens that do not exist per tailor palette). Known deviations from upstream, deliberate: list rows do not end-align their last child (luz gotcha 14), row/table hover uses the palette's --t-selection instead of luz's near-black --table-hover-bg (gotcha 13), warning ink is mixed 55% toward --t-text so orange shades stay readable (gotcha 25). Light palettes get surfaces slightly darker than the page (the dark-mode depth direction) — accepted approximation.

skins.name: Pico CSS
skins.description: Pico CSS 2.1.1's look (soft, rounded, generous spacing, solid primary, shadowed cards) translated onto the t-* vocabulary. Pico's --pico-* variables are bridged to --t-* tokens so every palette flows through.
skins.notes: Not vendored: pico.classless.min.css styles bare elements (dialog as a full-screen overlay, details/summary chevrons, nav li padding, button width 100 % in forms) and cannot be aliased onto read-only tailor markup (contract rule 5). skin.css re-declares Pico's metrics and visual rules against t-* selectors and keeps a --pico-* → --t-* bridge in :root so projects mixing Pico variables stay on-palette.

skins.name: Simple.css (translated)
skins.description: Simple.css's classless look on the t-* vocabulary: flat surfaces, 1px borders everywhere, one solid-accent button, zebra tables, boxed details/pre/notice, uniform 5px radius, no shadows. Deliberately more austere than the pico skin.
skins.notes: Translated, not vendored: Simple styles bare elements page-wide (body document grid, 3rem h1, every <button> accent-filled, every <td> bordered), which cannot be aliased onto tailor markup without breaking core/layout.css. Its 12 variables are bridged as private --s-* helpers (--s-bg → --t-canvas, --s-accent-bg → --t-inset, --s-accent → --t-accent-solid, --s-disabled → --t-selection …). Simple has no tabs, badges, toasts, menus, sidebar, switch or status colours; those are composed in its idiom (bordered pills, accent-bg boxes, a 3px tone bar on notices/toasts/toned rows).

skins.name: Tufte CSS (translated)
skins.description: Tufte CSS's long-form book look on the t-* vocabulary: et-book/Palatino serif, generous leading, weight-400 italic headings, hairline rules instead of boxes, no fills, no shadows, 2px corners. App components Tufte never had (buttons, forms, badges, toasts, dialogs, switches) are printed labels: thin tone-coloured rules and italics, never loud fills.
skins.notes: Translated, not vendored: tufte.css styles bare elements page-wide (body width/padding, 15px root, 1.4rem paragraphs, 55 % measure, sidenote counters) and has no controls, tables cells, nav or dialog, so nothing can be aliased onto tailor markup. Fonts: the stack leads with the et-book family names (et-book, 'ET Book') and falls back to Palatino / Palatino Linotype / Book Antiqua / Georgia / serif; the et-book woff files (MIT) are NOT shipped here — a project wanting the real face adds the four @font-face rules itself. Links inherit the ink and are underlined (Tufte); --t-link appears only on hover. Semantic tones stay distinguishable as tone-coloured hairlines/text, never washes. Dark palettes read as Tufte's own dark mode (colour-only swap).

skins.name: WebTUI (terminal look)
skins.description: Terminal/TUI rendering of the tailor vocabulary: monospace character grid, ch/lh rhythm, square corners, 2px frames, inverse-video selection, bracket checkboxes, braille spinner. WebTUI's attribute rules translated onto t-* selectors (nothing imported).
skins.notes: Translation, not a vendoring: the relevant @webtui/css 0.1.10 rules (box utility, button, badge, input, checkbox/radio/switch, spinner, progress, dialog, table) were rewritten on t-* selectors with --t-* colours; WebTUI's --background0..3/--foreground0..2/--box-border-color are bridged to --t-* for projects that add WebTUI markup alongside. Known WebTUI gotchas deliberately not carried over: body word-break:break-all, dialog position:absolute, 3lh default buttons. Badge/button text on a tone fill uses --t-canvas (WebTUI's background0 convention), so it depends on the palette's tone-vs-canvas contrast.

palettes.name: Gruvbox Dark (medium)
palettes.license: values-only (no LICENSE file in the repo)
